children: QatarEnergy is negotiating with several producers including Venture Global
to secure long-term U.S. liquefied natural gas contracts through 2031 to replace capacity knocked out by Iranian attacks that will ​take years to repair, Reuters reported Friday.

The discussions would mark a shift from QatarEnergy's purchases ​of dozens of U.S. spot LNG cargoes to help meet commitments to some of its ⁠Asian clients, suggesting it is now seeking longer-term solutions to cover the shortfall.

The contract reportedly talks are part of Qatar's attempts to replace lost volumes from its Ras Laffan facility after two of its 14 LNG trains and a gas-to-liquids facility were damaged by Iranian ​strikes in March.
After halting production, QatarEnergy has renewed force majeure notices monthly, most recently extended to November, with further extensions possible as the Strait of Hormuz remains closed.

Qatar's pursuit of long-term LNG volumes from other producers to help fulfill customer contracts "indicates that Qatar now sees ​risk to their ability to ​export LNG for several ⁠years," MST Marquee head of energy research Saul Kavonic told Reuters.

title: QatarEnergy in talks with Venture Global, others for U.S. LNG deals - Reuters
